title: Design for the Cast Iron Gate of Castle ‘s-Gravenwezel (Belgium)
creator: Jan Pieter van Baurscheidt the Younger
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Edward Pearce Casey Fund, 2016 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Pen and grey wash elevation of a cast-iron estate gate with two urn-topped piers and scrollwork. Symmetric, clean, centered; cream paper so easy luminance key. Use whole gate as the garden gate hero or split piers and gate leaf into layers.

title: The door of a grotto
creator: William Marlow
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, Jeffrey L. Berenson and Raymond Lifchez Living Trust Gifts, 2014 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: William Marlow watercolour: the door of a grotto set into craggy rock. A real grotto entrance in soft blue and ochre; vignette edge on paper, so key by paper tone and soften the edge.

title: Fishermen by Moonlight
creator: Joseph Vernet
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1953 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Blue-toned aquatint of fishermen by a moonlit river bank with a big tree and cottage, c. 1750-1800. Soft teal with a lit moon: tree and water layers could be separated. Small figures in a boat.

title: 'De Fontein van de Koninglijke door-eengevlochte Naam; voor de veiver', in: Tooneel Der Voornaamste Nederlands Huizen, En Lust Hoven, Naar T Leven Afgebeeld
creator: Carel Allard
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1937 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hand-coloured print of a sunken stepped basin fountain in a park. Soft rose, green and blue tints; has book spine and margins, crop to the plate.

title: Design for a Gate
creator: Anonymous, French, 18th century
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Harvard Arnason, 1971 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Fine pen and wash elevation of a gate between two rusticated piers with an ironwork overthrow and cartouche. Very clean outline, plain cream ground, easy cutout. Piers can be a separate layer from the iron leaf.

title: A Fountain in a Grotto
creator: Giovanni Guerra
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, James A. and Maria R. Warth Gift, in memory of Anne and Peter Warth, 1999 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Brown wash drawing of a fountain in a shell-niched grotto with rusticated surround, octagonal sheet. Warm and strong silhouette; contains reclining figures as sculpture, crop or paint out if needed.

title: Tintern Abbey by moonlight
creator: John "Warwick" Smith
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, Malcolm Hewitt Wiener Foundation and Jill Newhouse Gifts, 2003 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Tintern Abbey by moonlight, tinted print c. 1789: ruin on a hillside over a river with gentle moon glow. Calm background layer; no foreground figures that matter.

title: Design for a Cartouche, plate 2 from "Neü inventierte sehr dienstiche Schilde oder Cartouches"
creator: Jeremias Wachsmuth
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, Daniel Ergmann Gift, 2014 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hofer rococo cartouche with an empty centre, plate printed c. 1750-56, in an album with a leather edge to crop. Symmetric empty frame ready for label text.

title: Design for Gate Piers with Paired Pilasters and Domed Caps, and a Gate
creator: Anonymous, British, 18th century
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Elisha Whittelsey Collection, The Elisha Whittelsey Fund, 1949 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Faint wash design for gate piers with domed caps and a spear-topped iron leaf. Light line weight so it needs a strong levels pass; shape is simple and elegant for a small side gate.

title: View of a Palace Garden with a Central Pond Surrounded by Classical Architecture (Tapestry or Stage Design?)
creator: Daniel Marot the Elder
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, Brooke Russell Astor Bequest, 2013 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Watercolour of a palace garden seen between columns with urns and statue plinths on balustraded terraces. Tinted, painterly, usable as a mid-ground layer; urns and balustrade could be harvested. Statues are minor figures.

title: View of the Menagerie at Kew
creator: Thomas Sandby
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1925 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Watercolour View of the Menagerie at Kew (1763): a small pagoda pavilion on a curved pond edge with trees, pale blue wash water. Pond edge, reflection and pavilion in one; vignette edge, plain paper around.

title: Design for a Cartouche, plate 6 from "Neü inventierte sehr dienstiche Schilde oder Cartouches"
creator: Jeremias Wachsmuth
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, Daniel Ergmann Gift, 2014 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hofer rococo cartouche, empty centre, shell crest. Album page with leather edge; the frame is isolated on paper.

title: Bronze Garden Vase with Two Putti from the Gardens of Versailles
creator: Claude Ballin the Elder
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Edward Pearce Casey Fund, 2014 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Pen and grey wash drawing of a bronze garden vase with two putti, from the gardens of Versailles. Plain paper, centered object, clean silhouette: ideal urn on a pier. Faint grid lines in the paper to remove.

title: Study of a Tree in the Luxembourg Gardens
creator: Pierre Henri de Valenciennes
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Purchase, The Isaacson-Draper Foundation Gift, 2014 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Red-chalk study of a forked trunk in the Luxembourg Gardens, 1773. Foreground framing trunk candidate with branching top; warm red already fits the palette. Mounted in a gold-edged mat: crop it.

title: Trade Card of John Roker, Goldsmith
creator: Anonymous, British, 18th century
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Mrs. Morris Hawkes, 1927 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Trade card with an ornamental border and urn, framing a text block (John Roker). Ephemera feel; keep the border and urn, blank the text for a plant label or card.

title: Design for a Grotto with a Fountain
creator: Anonymous, Italian, 17th century
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Elisha Whittelsey Collection, The Elisha Whittelsey Fund, 1961 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Pen and wash design for a grotto niche with a tiered fountain, touched with blue wash on the water. Rusticated stone arch is a grotto entrance candidate; stained paper, plain around the object.

title: Vauxhall Garden
creator: Thomas Rowlandson
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1917 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hand-coloured aquatint of Vauxhall Garden lit at night, lanterns glowing under tall trees (1809). Dark sky, warm lights: strong mood plate. Tiny strolling figures are present, small and period; use as far-background or crop to trees and pavilion.

title: The Villa Torlonia, from the original painting by Joseph Castiglione in the collection of Mrs. A. T. Stewart, New York
creator: Edmond Yon
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Mrs. Ellen Robinson, 1960 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Villa Torlonia engraving with a pond edged by a stone balustrade under big trees. Dense dark foliage mass; balustrade and pond usable as a foreground. Contains a few seated figures.

title: Doorway and Vine
creator: James McNeill Whistler (American, 1834–1903)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Ralph King (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Whistler etching of a dark vaulted doorway through a vine-covered wall into light beyond. Mood piece for a wall opening: cut out the arch as an alpha hole or keep as a dark passage layer. Mid cutout difficulty.

title: The Doorway
creator: James McNeill Whistler (American, 1834–1903)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Bequest of James Parmelee (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Whistler etching of an arched lattice (trellis) doorway in a stone wall. Good as a garden doorway or arbour entrance; the lattice is fine detail so edges need care. Portrait format.

title: The Garden
creator: James McNeill Whistler (American, 1834–1903)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Ralph King (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Whistler etching The Garden: weathered door at the top of garden steps. Usable for door plus steps; heavy plate-tone so key by luminance and keep the paper warm.

title: The Fountains of Rome (Le fontane di Roma), Book IV, plate 21: View of the Cascade below the Organ from the Garden (Veduta della Cascata Sotto L'Organo nel Piano del Giardino)
creator: Giovanni Francesco Venturini (Italian, 1650–1710)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Jean Corser (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Venturini etching from Le fontane di Roma: a cascade falling from a grotto-like wall in a garden under trees. Full-sheet scene with plain margin; strong for fountain or grotto mood. Black-and-white, would be tinted.

title: Cedar (Cedrus sp.): tree with separate segments of cones and leaves. Coloured engraving by J.J. or J.E. Haid, c.1750, after G.D.Ehret.
creator: Georg Dionysius Ehret
attribution: Wellcome Collection, Public Domain Mark 1.0
notes: Hand-coloured engraving of a cedar of Lebanon with cones and seed scales around it, on plain paper. Beautiful conifer silhouette with horizontal tiers; cones can be used as separate hanging ornaments. Easy cutout.

title: Oak tree (Quercus hindsii) with person lying at its base. Coloured lithograph, c.1857.
creator: Unknown
attribution: Wellcome Collection, Public Domain Mark 1.0
notes: Chromolithograph of a broad oak tree in warm autumn gold with a second tree behind, plain pale ground. Soft rich colour, big open canopy, trunk visible: good single tree for perching birds. Paper key then clean the grass base.

title: An old oak tree (Quercus robur) with surrounding vegetation. Lithograph, c. 1822.
creator: Unknown
attribution: Wellcome Collection, Public Domain Mark 1.0
notes: Lithograph of an old oak with open, twisted branching and visible sky gaps, on plain paper (corner dog-ear and page edge to trim). Good silhouette for swallows; monochrome so tint by layer.

title: The Physic Garden, Chelsea: a view towards the river showing the cedars by the wall. Lithograph by H. Warren after J. Fuge.
creator: Fuge, James, -1838.
attribution: Wellcome Collection, Public Domain Mark 1.0
notes: Lithograph: south view of the cedars of Lebanon in the Apothecaries Physic Garden at Chelsea, flat layered crowns along a path. A garden-tree scene with a plain paper margin; the two big cedars can be cut from the ground.

title: Monterey Cypress
creator: Ernest Haskell (American, 1876–1925)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Bequest of Mrs. Henry A. Everett for the Dorothy Burnham Everett Memorial Collection (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Lithograph of two gnarled, wind-bent bare cypress trees on tan paper. Strange and open branching, ideal perches; dark ink on toned paper so key by luminance.

title: The Cypress Grove
creator: Samuel Palmer (British, 1805–1881)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Lewis B. Williams, presented in honor of Henry Sayles Francis, Curator of Prints (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Etching of a dark cypress and cedar grove with a stream. Heavy dark masses for silhouette trees at the garden edge; dense so cutout is mostly a luminance key and mass shape.

title: Eight Views of Kanazawa at Night
creator: Utagawa Hiroshige (Japanese, 1797–1858)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of Mrs. Francis F. Prentiss for the Dudley P. Allen Collection (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hiroshige triptych of Kanazawa at night: low islands in a bay under a full moon, deep blue woodblock gradients. Wide far-background layer, 3 panels that join; soft colour, no text beyond cartouches.

title: The Monkey Bridge
creator: Katsushika Taito II (Japanese, active c. 1810–50s)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift from J. H. Wade (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Woodblock of an arched Monkey Bridge under a full moon over a river gorge, early 1830s. Blue night colour with a moon disc behind the arch: reads as a ready moonlit window shot.

title: Moonlight on the Medway at Chatham
creator: Frank Short (British, 1857–1945)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Gift of John Bonebrake (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Mezzotint-style Moonlight on the Medway: warm sepia night sky with a moon, dark shore and a sail. Quiet, low-key far layer that holds colour tinting well.

title: Cedar trees (Cedrus species) in a garden in Monmouthshire. Photogravure by R. Fenton, ca. 1856.
creator: Roger Fenton
attribution: Wellcome Collection, Public Domain Mark 1.0
notes: Engraving of cedar trees reflected in a still pond (Cedrus, 1856). Clean water reflection on plain paper, monochrome, good for a pond layer with a tree beside it.

title: New Model for a Cartouche
creator: Stefano Della Bella (Italian, 1610–1664)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Dudley P. Allen Fund (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Stefano della Bella sheet of twelve empty cartouches and frames, 1647. Black ink on plain paper, each frame separable by grid; ideal for plant-label frames and Herbario cards.

title: Design for a Cartouche
creator: Gilles Marie Oppenord (French, 1672–1742)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, L. E. Holden Fund (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Oppenord red-chalk design for a cartouche: tall asymmetrical scrolls, warm red already in palette. Slim edge frame; plain paper.

title: Old Cypress Trees in Carthusian Convent, Rome
creator: Jane Martha St. John
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gilman Collection, Gift of The Howard Gilman Foundation, 2005 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: 1850s albumen photograph of two tall columnar cypresses in a Carthusian cloister garden, Rome (Jane Martha St. John), with a pencil caption below. Classic cypress silhouettes against cloister arches; sepia tone; sky is plain pale so a luminance key separates the trees, crop caption.

title: Cypress Bower
creator: Ernest Haskell (American, 1876–1925)
attribution: The Cleveland Museum of Art, Dudley P. Allen Fund (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Etching Cypress Bower: wind-swept dark cypress canopies over a clearing, cream paper. Dense dark masses, use as a silhouette tree cluster at the garden edge; plate border and signature to crop.

title: Labyrinte de Versailles
creator: Isaac de Benserade
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1931 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Labyrinthe de Versailles (1677) engraving: a clipped-hedge tunnel with an arched opening and statue plinths, on plain paper inside a plate mark. A hedge archway for foreground framing or a green door; statues are small garden sculpture. Black and white, would be tinted green.

title: 'De Laan na Ceres, tegen over 't Beeld van Phaunus'', in: Tooneel Der Voornaamste Nederlands Huizen, En Lust Hoven, Naar T Leven Afgebeeld
creator: Carel Allard
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1937 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hand-coloured print of a long tree-lined avenue ending in a niche arch, from a bound Dutch garden book. Soft greens and rose; clipped lime avenue would give hedge and tree rows. Book margins and leather edge to crop; small figures.

title: ' ’De Koninginne Tuin met 't Groene Kabinet , en de Oranjerie, van Achteren gezien", in: Tooneel Der Voornaamste Nederlands Huizen, En Lust Hoven, Naar T Leven Afgebeeld
creator: Carel Allard
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1937 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hand-coloured view of a formal garden with clipped orange trees in tubs and a long orangery, from a Dutch garden book. Topiary and parterre in delicate colour; bound-book margins to crop; tiny figures.

title: 'De Cascade van Narcissus, aan de Oost-zyde van de Groote Tuin', in: Tooneel Der Voornaamste Nederlands Huizen, En Lust Hoven, Naar T Leven Afgebeeld
creator: Carel Allard
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1937 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hand-coloured print of a stepped stone cascade (Cascade of Narcissus) with urns and a central statue in a garden, from a Dutch garden book. Coloured stone and water, fountain with urns. Book margins to crop; people at the sides are small.

title: 'Het Groote Doolhof', in: Tooneel Der Voornaamste Nederlands Huizen, En Lust Hoven, Naar T Leven Afgebeeld
creator: Carel Allard
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Harris Brisbane Dick Fund, 1937 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Hand-coloured print of the entrance pavilions and open gate to a garden labyrinth (Het Groote Doolhof) with hedge walls behind. Garden entrance layer; book margins to crop; several small figures at the gate.

title: View of a Garden with a Water Basin and Large Fountain, title page from "Grottes et fontaines de jardins à l'italienne"
creator: Jean Le Pautre
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Bequest of Phyllis Massar, 2011 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: 17th-century engraving of a garden with a large round water basin carrying a fountain group, balustraded terraces and hedged walls, topped by a cartouche. Reflective basin plus balustrade and cartouche, plain paper margins; the fountain group has putti and sea figures as sculpture.

title: Hieracium Pilosella in Billings-Kittredge Herbaria (herbarium sheet)
creator: Billings-Kittredge Herbaria, Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park (imaging by Boston Photo Imaging)
institution: National Park Service, via NPGallery and Wikimedia Commons
attribution: Billings-Kittredge Herbaria, Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP, National Park Service (public domain), via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Early-1900s herbarium sheet (collected 1919): mouse-ear hawkweed pressed with rosette and flower head on foxed paper, typed label and herbarium stamp lower right. Warm cream sheet with torn edge; plant cut by luminance key against paper; label can be a separate card layer.

title: Brassica Arvensis in Billings-Kittredge Herbaria (herbarium sheet)
creator: Billings-Kittredge Herbaria, Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park (imaging by Boston Photo Imaging)
institution: National Park Service, via NPGallery and Wikimedia Commons
attribution: Billings-Kittredge Herbaria, Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP, National Park Service (public domain), via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Herbarium sheet (1928) of a tall pressed charlock stem with pods on aged paper, label at bottom. Slender silhouette good for a vertical Herbario card; label text is real handwriting and typed text, keep as texture.

title: Antennaria Canadensis in Billings-Kittredge Herbaria (herbarium sheet)
creator: Billings-Kittredge Herbaria, Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park (imaging by Boston Photo Imaging)
institution: National Park Service, via NPGallery and Wikimedia Commons
attribution: Billings-Kittredge Herbaria, Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP, National Park Service (public domain), via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Herbarium sheet (1911) with pressed pussytoes flower tuft on a long stem and basal leaves, soft fluffy head. Very airy silhouette; delicate fluff needs careful keying. Label bottom right.

title: Carex Trichocarpa in Billings-Kittredge Herbaria (herbarium sheet)
creator: Billings-Kittredge Herbaria, Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park (imaging by Boston Photo Imaging)
institution: National Park Service, via NPGallery and Wikimedia Commons
attribution: Billings-Kittredge Herbaria, Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP, National Park Service (public domain), via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Herbarium sheet (1920) of long curving sedge blades and seed spikes on a damaged brown-tan sheet with chipped corner. Graphic sweeping lines; good as a background herbarium texture with torn edges.

title: Panicum Lindheimeri in Billings-Kittredge Herbaria (herbarium sheet)
creator: Billings-Kittredge Herbaria, Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller National Historical Park (imaging by Boston Photo Imaging)
institution: National Park Service, via NPGallery and Wikimedia Commons
attribution: Billings-Kittredge Herbaria, Marsh-Billings-Rockefeller NHP, National Park Service (public domain), via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Herbarium sheet (1923) of a branching pressed grass-like plant with narrow leaves and airy flower sprays on stained paper with a torn corner and a typed label.

title: Herbarium sheet, Malva alcea (collector Marcel Etringer)
creator: Marcel Etringer (collector); scan by Musee national d'histoire naturelle Luxembourg
institution: Musee national d'histoire naturelle Luxembourg (Herbarium LUX)
attribution: Herbarium sheet Malva alcea (Marcel Etringer), Musee national d'histoire naturelle Luxembourg, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Herbarium sheet of vervain mallow with a pink bloom, original collector label and a pasted handwritten tag. Sheet carries a colour scale bar and barcode on the right edge: crop them off. Warm paper, nice foliage.

title: "A Wish" postcard (1913), reverse
creator: Unknown publisher (scan by AWB)
institution: Wikimedia Commons (scan of a card at Antique Village, Hanover, VA)
attribution: "A Wish" postcard (1913) reverse, scan by AWB, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Reverse of a 1913 postcard: ornate art-nouveau POST CARD heading, divided message and address areas, stamp box, tiny printer mark bottom left. Almost blank grey-cream card: usable as a Herbario card back or a postcard prop; heading can be kept as period type.

title: Antique vase (from Vasi, candelabri, cippi, sarcofagi, tripodi, lucerne, ed ornamenti antichi), RP-P-OB-39.601
creator: Giovanni Battista Piranesi
attribution: Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, RP-P-OB-39.601 (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Piranesi etching (1778) of a large marble Medici-type krater urn with acanthus and relief band on a fluted base, plain cream paper, caption lettering below. Superb garden urn for a pier; strong silhouette, easy paper key, crop caption. Rijksmuseum, 4000+ px original (downloaded at 3840 wide).

title: Candelabrum, cippi and vase (from Vasi, candelabri, cippi, sarcofagi, tripodi, lucerne, ed ornamenti antichi), RP-P-OB-39.641
creator: Giovanni Battista Piranesi
attribution: Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, RP-P-OB-39.641 (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Piranesi etching sheet of an ornate stone candelabrum with sphinx-footed base, two cippi tablets and urns around it, on white paper. Tall stone column to harvest as garden obelisk or pedestal; Latin captions are part of the engraving, crop or cover.

title: Tripod or altar (from Vasi, candelabri, cippi, sarcofagi, tripodi, lucerne, ed ornamenti antichi), RP-P-OB-39.610
creator: Giovanni Battista Piranesi
attribution: Rijksmuseum, Amsterdam, RP-P-OB-39.610 (CC0), via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Piranesi etching of a carved marble tripod altar with garlands and winged forms, text column at left. Heavy stone ornament for a sundial plinth or garden altar; paper plain and warm. Contains small carved griffin or sphinx figures, no human bodies.

title: Ribbon
creator: Bon Marché
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Brooklyn Museum Costume Collection at The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of the Brooklyn Museum, 2009; Gift of Amelia Beard Hollenback, 1966 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Costume Institute photograph of three silk ribbon lengths (ochre stripes, green and cream plaid, red and tan stripes) on black, 1880s. Satin sheen, saturated yet soft; keys cleanly off the black. Cut the three bands apart for cords and ties.

title: Ribbon
creator: European
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Brooklyn Museum Costume Collection at The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of the Brooklyn Museum, 2009; Gift of Adelaide Goan, 1955 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Photograph on black of a 19th-century woven silk ribbon with red roses and small blossoms on a green ground, folded in an S. Usable as a ribbon tie or garland; black key is easy, edges slightly frayed.

title: Ribbon
creator: Unknown
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Brooklyn Museum Costume Collection at The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of the Brooklyn Museum, 2009; Museum Expedition 1920 & 1921, Robert B. Woodward Memorial Fund, 1921 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Photograph on black of an early 19th-century orange and brown patterned ribbon folded in a Z. Warm ochre ribbon for tags and plant labels; clean black ground.

title: Book Label for Mrs. Judith Hackam
creator: Anonymous, British, 18th century
attribution: The Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gift of Bella C. Landauer, 1926 (Open Access, CC0)
notes: Printed book label with a typographic border of printer's flowers and a framed centre panel, 18th-century type (Mrs. Judith Hackam in manuscript, Oxford 1731). A ready plant-label or specimen-tag stock: keep the border, blank the manuscript name. Small image, crop tight.

title: "Welcome Utah" statehood postcard, reverse
creator: Unknown publisher (scan by Familypapers)
attribution: "Welcome Utah" postcard reverse, scan by Familypapers, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Reverse of an early 1900s postcard with big teal outlined POST CARD lettering, stamp box and divided back, on warm cream stock. Blank writing area, teal printing sits well with the palette.

title: Real-photo postcard, reverse (Frankford Old Home Week souvenir)
creator: Unknown
attribution: 1909 RPPC postcard reverse, unknown author, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Reverse of a 1909 real-photo postcard on brown card stock with faint printed POST CARD, AZO-style stamp box and divided lines. Darker brown tone suits dusk scenes. Hand number in pencil top right.

title: Postcard reverse, Schloss Dobrilugk-Kirchhain
creator: Albert Kien, Dobrilugk (publisher)
attribution: 1925 postcard reverse, Albert Kien, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Reverse of a 1925 German postcard: pale yellow stock, only fine divider and address lines, almost completely blank. Cleanest blank card back; edges are straight so no cutout needed.

title: Postkarte reverse, Zeughaus Berlin series Nr. 267
creator: Julius Bard Verlag for the Koenigliche Zeughaus-Verwaltung, Berlin
attribution: Circa 1900 Postkarte reverse, Julius Bard Verlag, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Reverse of a c. 1900 German Postkarte: salmon-pink card with a black eagle masthead and stamp box, blank message area. Printed text at left is real publisher text, crop or cover.

title: Alice in Wonderland (1915 film), title card
creator: Unknown (1915 silent film, Internet Archive copy)
attribution: Alice in Wonderland (1915) title card, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Title-card frame from the 1915 silent film Alice in Wonderland: sepia-toned hand-drawn lettering and small Alice and White Rabbit vignette on a dark brown card. Direct reference for intertitle style; lettering must be replaced with own text, art can be reused as a corner ornament.

title: Cinema advertising slide: "Advertise your business on this screen"
creator: Miscellaneous Items in High Demand, Prints and Photographs, Library of Congress
institution: Library of Congress (LCCN 2012645958), via Wikimedia Commons
attribution: Library of Congress, LCCN 2012645958, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Library of Congress silent-era cinema advertising slide: ornate silvered rounded frame with floral border around a horse portrait and centred text on black. The frame is a ready intertitle border; replace the text, and drop the horse for the portrait window.

title: Red woven band (NM.0048258A)
creator: Elisabeth Eriksson (photographer); object in Nordiska museet
attribution: Elisabeth Eriksson / Nordiska museet, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Museum photograph of a red woven ribbon band with patterned ends and fringe on white. Soft pure red fits the palette; background is plain white so keying is trivial. Real object, 19th-century folk textile (Nordiska museet), CC BY 4.0 attribution required.

title: Patterned woven band with tassels (NM.0003516B)
creator: Elisabeth Eriksson (photographer); object in Nordiska museet
attribution: Elisabeth Eriksson / Nordiska museet, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Museum photograph of a long red patterned woven band, coiled, with dried-flower and silk tassels at the ends, on white. Great silk-cord prop for tags and plant labels; cut out against white, tassels need soft edges. CC BY 4.0 (Nordiska museet).

title: Excess luggage ticket, London and South Western Railway
creator: Unknown (London and South Western Railway)
institution: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NARA 278330)
attribution: National Archives and Records Administration, NARA 278330, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: National Archives scan of a 1912 London and South Western Railway excess luggage ticket: pale green card with printed form, gold brass eyelets and pencil handwriting. Real tag-like ephemera in green that suits viridian; handwritten name should be blanked.

title: Garden Gate
creator: Thomas Morris
institution: Yale Center for British Art, B1977.14.18430
attribution: Yale Center for British Art, B1977.14.18430, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: Etching titled Garden Gate (Thomas Morris, Yale Center for British Art): a wrought-iron double gate with spiked piers and an overthrow scroll set between two big trees, plain cream sheet. Exactly the garden gate; iron tracery is fine so cut by luminance, tree canopy at the sides can be split off.

title: North Side of Garden Gate (Xiyanglou series)
creator: Qing court painters; engraved by the Zaobanchu workshop
institution: Old Summer Palace (Xiyanglou) set of twenty copperplate engravings, via Wikimedia Commons
attribution: North Side of Garden Gate, 1786, Qing court, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
notes: 1786 drawing of a walled garden seen frontally with an ornate pavilion-gate in the centre wall and pruned trees on both sides; light line work on pale paper with a few small inscriptions at the right edge. A symmetric walled-garden gate view; delicate lines need a strong levels pass.

title: Venus's Fly-trap (Dionaea muscipula), hand-coloured engraved plate
creator: John Ellis (author), engraved by James Roberts
institution: Wikimedia Commons, from the Hunt Institute for Botanical Documentation (Carnegie Mellon University) copy of Ellis's letter to Linnaeus
attribution: Ellis, J. (1769). Venus's Fly-trap, Dionaea muscipula. Engraved by James Roberts, hand-coloured. Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
notes: One plate with a tall flowering stalk, a rosette of leaves and several traps seen open from the front and from the side, with a fly. Pale paper with faint show-through text from the verso. Cut by hand into the flytrap boss rig: the stalk with its flowers, three leaves, and the front-open trap split along its hinge into two lobes.
